nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_utils module

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_utils.find_temp_offset(heights: list[float] | ndarray) → float[source]

If data has near vertical or horizontal features, this function returns an offset computed from the widest valley using inverted peak detection.

This is useful for determining the appropriate rotation angle to align features in the data.

Parameters:

heights (list of float or np.ndarray) – 1D array of histogram bin heights.

Returns:

angle_of_valley – The angle corresponding to the widest valley in the histogram. If no valleys are found, returns 0 indicating no shift is needed.

Return type:

float

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_PCA module

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_PCA.orientation_via_PCA(binary_image, line_length=20, num_neighbors=50)[source]

Compute local orientation via PCA for each point in a binary image.

Uses a chaining method to build a local neighbourhood for each point: starting from each point, greedily extends a chain of nearby unvisited neighbours and fits PCA to determine the dominant local direction.

Parameters:

  • binary_image (np.ndarray) – Binary image where True values represent points of interest.

  • line_length (int, optional) – Number of points to include in each local chain/subgroup. Default is 20. More number leads to more accurate results, but also increases the processing time. Less number decreases processing time but makes the estimation vulnerable to errors cause by non-linearly oriented features.

  • num_neighbors (int, optional) – Number of nearest neighbours to query when extending/creating the local chain. Higher values reduce the chance of getting stuck. Default is 50..

Returns:

  • point_orientations (np.ndarray) – 2-D float array of the same shape as binary_image. Each foreground pixel carries its local orientation in degrees (wrapped to [0, 180)); background pixels are NaN.

  • angle_profile (np.ndarray) – histogram of the angle scores detected by ‘pca’

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Probabilistic module

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Probabilistic.label_points_by_angle(x, y, theta_degs, bin_width=1.0, tol=1.5, min_peak_prominence=5)[source]

Assign each point to its closest trackline family across all dominant angles.

For each image-convention angle φ in theta_degs the function converts back to the sinogram projection angle (φ + 90°) so that points on the same trackline produce the same ρ value, then finds trackline centers in ρ-space via a histogram peak search. Each point is assigned to the angle family whose nearest trackline center is closest; points whose best distance exceeds tol are labelled −1.

Parameters:

  • x (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • y (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • theta_degs (array-like) – Image-convention dominant angles in degrees (as returned by compute_local_orientation_via_radon after the −90° correction).

  • bin_width (float) – Histogram bin width in pixels for the ρ projection.

  • tol (float) – Maximum ρ-distance from a trackline center to count as membership.

  • min_peak_prominence (float) – Passed to scipy.signal.find_peaks; tune to point density.

Returns:

  • labels (np.ndarray of int) – Per-point index into theta_degs (i.e. the assigned angle family), or −1 if the point is unassigned.

  • all_peak_centers (list of np.ndarray) – Refined ρ trackline centers for each angle in theta_degs.

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Probabilistic.label_points_by_probabilistic_line(x, y, theta_degs, bin_width=1.0, tol=5, num_neighbors=5, chain_length=100, n_times=3)[source]

Assign each point a local angle orientation using probabilistic line fitting.

Runs a multi-vote ensemble: the core algorithm is repeated until every point has been visited at least n_times, and the final label is the angle family that received the most votes (mode). Points that are always near a trackline boundary get their correct family reinforced across independent random probes, suppressing one-off mislabels.

Parameters:

  • x (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • y (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • theta_degs (array-like) – Image-convention dominant angles in degrees (as returned by compute_local_orientation_via_radon after the −90° correction).

  • bin_width (float) – Maximum perpendicular distance (pixels) from the fitted line for a point to be considered part of that line segment. Default is 1.0.

  • tol (float) – Maximum angular difference (degrees) between the PCA-computed angle and the nearest entry in theta_degs for the snap to be accepted. Probes that cannot be snapped cast no vote. Default is 5.

  • num_neighbors (int) – Number of nearest neighbours queried at each chain-extension step. Higher values reduce the chance of getting stuck. Default is 20.

  • chain_length (int) – Maximum number of points in each local chain used for PCA. Default 10.

  • n_times (int) – Minimum number of votes each point must accumulate before the loop terminates. Higher values reduce mislabels at the cost of runtime. Default is 3.

Returns:

  • labels (np.ndarray of int) – Per-point index into theta_degs (i.e. the winning angle family), or −1 if the point received no valid votes.

  • all_peak_centers (list) – Empty list; returned for API symmetry with label_points_by_angle. This method does not compute ρ-space trackline centers.

Notes

Steps (per iteration):

  1. Randomly select an under-labeled point from the foreground.

  2. Greedily chain chain_length nearest neighbours to build a local linear probe.

  3. Compute the mean inter-point distance along the chain.

4. Fit PCA to the chain; extract the dominant direction as an angle. 4a. Snap the angle to the closest entry in theta_degs (within tol);

discard the probe (no vote) if no entry is close enough.

  1. Find all foreground points within bin_width pixels perpendicular to the snapped line through the starting point.

  2. Flood-fill a connected segment from the starting point through the near-line set, using 2 × mean_dist as the adjacency radius.

  3. Cast one vote for the snapped angle family on every under-labeled point in the connected segment.

  4. Repeat until every point has been visited n_times.

  5. Resolve each point’s label as argmax of its vote histogram.

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Probabilistic.label_points_by_probabilistic_line2(x, y, theta_degs, bin_width=1.0, tol=5, num_neighbors=20, chain_length=10, min_tentative=5)[source]

Two-tier probabilistic line labeling without BFS connectivity.

Each randomly selected point receives a definitive label from its local PCA angle (snapped to a Radon-detected family). Every point that lies within bin_width pixels of that line receives one tentative vote for the same family. The loop runs until every point has either been selected once or accumulated at least min_tentative tentative votes, whichever comes first. Final labels are the definitive label for selected points and the majority-vote angle for the rest.

Compared to label_points_by_probabilistic_line, this variant:

  • Removes the BFS connected-component step — near-line membership is a pure perpendicular-distance test, vectorised over all points.

  • Separates definitive (strong) from tentative (weak) evidence, so a point selected as a start always gets the label its own chain implies, while boundary points accumulate evidence from many passing probes.

Parameters:

  • x (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • y (array-like) – Column and row coordinates of foreground pixels.

  • theta_degs (array-like) – Image-convention dominant angles in degrees (Radon-detected).

  • bin_width (float) – Maximum perpendicular distance (pixels) for a point to receive a tentative vote from a passing line. Default is 1.0.

  • tol (float) – Maximum angular difference (degrees) between the PCA angle and the nearest theta_degs entry for the snap to be accepted. Default 5.

  • num_neighbors (int) – Nearest-neighbour count for each chain-extension query. Default 20.

  • chain_length (int) – Maximum chain length for PCA; start_idx sits near the middle via bidirectional growth. Default 10.

  • min_tentative (int) – Minimum tentative votes a non-selected point must receive before it is considered sufficiently labeled. Default 5.

Returns:

  • labels (np.ndarray of int) – Per-point index into theta_degs, or −1 if unresolved.

  • all_peak_centers (list) – Empty list; for API symmetry with label_points_by_angle.

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Probabilistic.orientation_via_probabilistic_line(binary_image: ndarray, test_angles: ndarray = None, circle: bool = True, tol: int | None = 5, precomputed_theta: dict = None) → dict[source]

Find the dominant orientation of linear features using the Radon transform.

Computes the Radon sinogram over test_angles and returns the angle whose projection column has the highest variance. High variance indicates that projections along that angle produce concentrated bright lines, which is characteristic of linear features aligned with that orientation.

Parameters:

  • image (np.ndarray) – Binary image containing linear features.

  • test_angles (np.ndarray, optional) – Angles in degrees at which to compute the Radon transform. If None, 180 angles uniformly spaced over [0°, 180°) are used.

  • circle (bool, optional) – If True, only pixels within the inscribed circle are projected (matches the skimage default). Default is True.

  • tol (int | None, optional) – Half-width in degrees of the suppression band around each angle in remove_angles. Default is 5.

Returns:

  • theta_info (dict) – Dictionary with keys:

    • 'peaks' : np.ndarray of float — dominant angle(s) in degrees, sorted by descending prominence.

    • 'widths_in_degrees' : np.ndarray of float — FWHM of each peak in degrees.

    • 'profile_variance' : np.ndarray of float — variance profile over all tested angles (rolled so index 0 corresponds to 0°).

  • angle_profile (np.ndarray) – histogram of the angle scores detected by ‘radon’

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Radon module

nbs_uncles.orientation.orientation_via_Radon.orientation_via_Radon(binary_image: ndarray, angle_info: dict = None, circle: bool = False, angular_tolerance: int = 5, width_tolerance: int = 5, min_intensity: float = 0.05, top_angles: int = 3, do_offset: bool = False, zoom_factor: float = 2.0, show_plot: bool = True)[source]

Find the dominant orientation of linear features using the Radon transform.

Computes the Radon sinogram over test_angles by computing for the angle whose projection column has the highest variance. High variance indicates that projections along that angle produce concentrated bright lines, suggesting presence of linear features aligned with that orientation.

Parameters:

  • binary_image (np.ndarray) – Binary image containing linear features.

  • angle_info (dict, optional) – theta_info returned by a previous call; reuses its sinogram and offset instead of recomputing the Radon transform.

  • circle (bool, optional) – If True, only pixels within the circle inscribed in the central square are projected — Set to False as we need to reconstruct the image using the original dimensions.

  • angular_tolerance (int | None, optional) – Half-width in degrees of the suppression band around each angle in remove_angles. Default is 5.

  • width_tolerance (int | None, optional) – minimum distance in pixels between two lines of the same family

  • min_intensity (float, optional) – Minimum intensity of a pixel to be considered part of a linear feature.

  • top_angles (int, optional) – Number of dominant angles to return. If set to 0, all detected angles are returned.

  • do_offset (bool, optional) – Set to ‘True’ if data has near vertical or horizontal features to offset for better peak detection. Default is False.

  • zoom_factor (float, optional) – Down-scaling factor applied before the Radon transform. Default is 2.0.

  • show_plot (bool, optional) – Draw the log profile variance figure. Default is True.

Returns:

  • point_orientations (dict) – {angle_deg: float_raster} with the pixels of each detected angle family, plus 'combined' holding all families. Background is NaN.

  • theta_info (dict) – {'theta', 'sinogram', 'temp_offset'}; pass it back as angle_info to skip the Radon transform on later calls.
